Civilian.name: Civilian
Civilian.description:
The ordinary people of Japan: office workers, shopkeepers, station staff, delivery drivers, nurses, reporters, retirees and the families of students and heroes. About four in five have a Quirk, registered at age four, and most Quirks are small and everyday: a knack that helps at work, a minor Mutant feature, a party trick. Public Quirk use without a hero license is illegal except in self-defense, so most people use their Quirks only in private. Heteromorph people face prejudice, and people with no Quirk face pity.

They follow the hero rankings, buy merchandise, film every fight on their phones and complain about property damage afterward. In danger they run, hide, help others out and call for heroes; a few freeze, and a few use a Quirk in self-defense. They are courteous and reserved with strangers, louder and quicker to joke in Osaka, and wary of anyone who uses a Quirk openly in public. A civilian with an everyday Quirk can be the one witness who noticed what mattered.

## Generating New NPCs
Civilians are adults; anyone who is still a minor takes the Child type and its rules. Families of canon characters (such as Inko Midoriya) are canon NPCs: never generate a relative of a canon character. Use a Japanese name, given name first, ordinary for the region (foreign only for visitors and residents from abroad), never a canon character's family name. Give an everyday Quirk with a clear scope and a real limit, or none (about one in five). They know only what the news, rumor and their own eyes tell them.

## Visual Description
Adults in the everyday clothes of modern Japan, suited to their work and the season: office suits, shop aprons, station and delivery uniforms, nurse's scrubs, casual weekend wear. Heteromorph features (animal heads, horns, scales, extra arms) are common and ordinary. No hero costumes, and no text or logos.
